ne123954d3efd: Chromosome replication initiation in bacterial genomes typically occurs at a single origin, called oriC, through the binding of the DnaA initiator protein to specific chromosomal repeats known as DnaA-boxes. Here, relying on comparative genomics, we show that the family Fusobacteriaceae, which belongs to the order Fusobacteriales alongside the family Leptotrichiaceae, deviates from this paradigm. Our analysis revealed a stark contrast between the two lineages: while dnaA flanks oriC in Leptotrichiaceae, it is notably missing from Fusobacteriaceae genomes. Adjacent to oriC in Fusobacteriaceae, we identified a gene encoding replication initiator protein A (RPA). We characterized RPA as a Rep-type initiator involved in plasmid replication that likely originated from an iteron-containing plasmid, iterons being the plasmid analogues of DnaA-boxes. Phylogenetic reconstruction indicates that the gene encoding RPA was acquired together with its associated iterons and subsequently domesticated by the Fusobacteriaceae ancestor, successfully displacing the ancestral chromosomal dnaA gene at the origin of replication. This shift to a plasmid-derived replication system may represent an adaptive trait of the Fusobacteriaceae, potentially offering new insights into the biology of Fusobacterium nucleatum, a member of this family known to be a major driver of colorectal cancer progression within the tumor microenvironment.
nafe97af1c2ad: Droplet-based and split-pool barcoding are the two dominant high-throughput single-cell RNA-seq paradigms, yet their systematic biases remain incompletely characterized. We compared seven matched 10X Genomics Chromium and Parse Biosciences Evercode WT sample pairs from five studies spanning multiple tissues and species focusing on gene counts and compositional differences rather than cell-type resolution. By separating Parse reads by priming strategy, we distinguished biases arising from priming chemistry from platform-level effects. These effects were largely independent, with platform-level differences substantially larger. Priming strategy introduced a GC-content bias within Parse, whereas the two platforms showed a consistent compositional shift across priming strategies, supported by differential capture of nuclear- and cytoplasmic-enriched transcripts. We interpret this shift as a relative enrichment of nuclear RNA in Parse. Finally, using contamination measures that do not assume a droplet-specific model, we found background RNA contamination in Parse to be comparable in magnitude to that in 10X, contrary to claims of substantially lower contamination. Together, these results indicate that expression measurements and cell-type composition are not directly interchangeable between the two platforms. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. nbf10ee8d07a1: A single nucleotide polymorphism (rs2304297) in the 3' untranslated region (UTR) of CHRNA6, encoding the alpha6 nicotinic acetylcholine receptor subunit, is associated with adolescent smoking behavior. Humanized rats carrying the 'C' or 'G' allele show sex- and genotype-dependent responses to adolescent nicotine, yet the variant does not alter the protein sequence and the mechanism has remained unknown. We examined the molecular consequences of rs2304297 in vivo in the adolescent ventral tegmental area (VTA). Chrna6 transcript abundance did not differ by genotype, nor did transcript stability or polyadenylation site selection. The variant was instead associated with a transcriptional signature spanning myelin maintenance (Enpp6), lipid metabolism (Retsat), and genomic repair (Polq), and with elevated basal lipid peroxidation in alpha6GG animals. Computational folding predicted greater conformational flexibility of the 'G' allele, and spatial colocalization of Chrna6 with miRNA-365-5p was reduced in alpha6GG animals of both sexes. Coordinated expression of the two transcripts, however, followed a sex-by-genotype pattern, absent in alpha6CC females and alpha6GG males. These same groups showed elevated tyrosine hydroxylase expression and dopaminergic neuron number, and expansion of the Chrna6 co-expression network following nicotine. We propose that rs2304297 acts through two distinct layers: genotype determines spatial engagement of miRNA-365-5p with the transcript, while sex determines whether that engagement produces functional regulation. These findings identify a post-transcriptional mechanism for a non-coding nicotine addiction risk variant and demonstrate that its molecular effect can be uniform while its consequences are not. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. na409e23c69b5: The choroid plexus (ChP) is a highly vascularized structure located in the brain ventricles that plays important roles in multiple central nervous system functions. ChP enlargement has been implicated in many neuropsychiatric conditions such as multiple sclerosis, depression, schizophrenia, and Alzheimer's disease. However, limitation in the accuracy of the current segmentation tools highlight the need for more reliable methods to quantify ChP volume in healthy and clinical human populations. The shape and size of the ChP vary drastically from person to person, and currently there are no large ChP datasets which allow comprehensive training of segmentation models. Here we introduce DataPlex, a collection of 700 structural MRI brain images where the lateral ventricle ChP has been manually labeled and checked by expert human raters. DataPlex is balanced and representative across a wide range of scanning parameters, demographics, and clinical profiles, and subject-level information will be available for each labeled image. DataPlex will be open source to support the creation of reliable segmentation tools for the human lateral ventricle ChP. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n85c10a852388: In this study, we develop a mathematical model of the hypothalamic pituitary adrenal (HPA) axis and systematically investigate the model complexity required to reproduce observed hormone dynamics. The model is fitted to ACTH and cortisol measurements from five healthy volunteers reported in the literature. We show that simultaneous reproduction of both hormone profiles requires a delay differential equation model with at least five state variables among the model architectures considered. Following fitting the volunteer data, we investigate the response of the model to sustained stress using bifurcation analysis. The coupled system exhibits bifurcations over a range of stress intensities. This analysis reveals bifurcations whose critical stress thresholds depend strongly on the modulatory state of the system. These results provide a mathematical framework for investigating transitions between physiological and dysregulated HPA axis dynamics, which may be related to states of health and disease. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
nd8f4e1d89f9c: Premise: : Conifers comprise one-sixth of global forests and landscape genomic studies are urgently needed to understand their biology, yet relatively few conifer species have reference genomes. Targeted exon-capture is a practical alternative to whole-genome sequencing, but selecting loci without a reference genome remains a barrier. We developed a multi-tissue reference transcriptome for pi ñon pine ( Pinus edulis ) to ask how multi-tissue sampling improves probe design, and what is lost under a conventional single-tissue approach. Methods: We assembled a reference transcriptome from four diploid tissues (needle, phloem, root, vegetative bud) and one haploid tissue (megagametophyte), using the latter as a pseudo-guide. We designed a target-capture probe-set by prioritizing highly expressed P. edulis transcripts and transcripts matching a conifer exon database. Results: We recovered 76% of conserved plant genes with few duplicated transcripts. Filtering yielded 15,664 transcripts totaling 31.4 Mb, ~0.1% of the genome. Tissue-specific expression was substantial: 27.4% of transcripts occurred exclusively in non-needle tissues. Functional annotation confirmed complementary contributions, including seed-desiccation and germination genes from megagametophytes, and defense- and stress-associated genes from roots and phloem. Discussion: We built a transcriptome and efficient probe set using a roadmap suitable for other non-model plants with large genomes; keys to success were prioritizing complementary tissues and using expression-based filtering.
ndc5fe997882a: RNA splicing is frequently disrupted by genetic variation, contributing to a wide range of human diseases. Identifying the variants responsible for altered splicing is therefore crucial but has long been challenging. Deep learning models that predict splicing from genomic sequence have substantially advanced their detection, but accurately resolving their quantitative effects on splicing and the resulting transcripts remains an unmet need. Here we introduce SpliceAI2, a deep learning model trained end-to-end on splice site, splice junction, and transcript usage across multiple mammalian species. SpliceAI2 reconstructs complete transcripts directly from genomic sequence and considerably improves identification of splice-altering variants and quantification of their effects in diverse benchmarks spanning cryptic splicing, splicing quantitative trait loci, and massively parallel reporter assays. Human population datasets provide independent validation of these predicted functional effects through evidence of natural selection and associated changes in plasma protein abundance. Application to a rare disease cohort reveals that predicted splice-altering variants are highly enriched in disease-associated genes and account for 15% of the excess genetic burden, with approximately half residing in deep intronic regions likely missed by exome sequencing. Together, these findings establish SpliceAI2 as a major step forward in interpreting splice-altering variants across the human genome.
n77498144b5c2: Alternating hemiplegia of childhood (AHC) is a rare neurodevelopmental disorder primarily caused by heterozygous de novo mutations in the ATP1A3 gene, which encodes the neuron-specific catalytic α3 subunit of the P-type Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase. Among these, the E815K variant is the second most frequent ATP1A3 mutation in AHC and is associated with the most severe clinical phenotypes, characterized by frequent epileptic and dystonic episodes and profound developmental impairment, making it a key target for mechanistic study. Although E815K was shown to disrupt pump function in heterologous systems and animal models, its impact on human neurons remain poorly understood. To investigate its disease-relevant pathophysiology, we generated induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) from an AHC patient carrying the E815K mutation and differentiated them into mature neurons. Patient-derived neurons displayed normal differentiation and synaptogenesis, with preserved evoked synaptic transmission. However, α3-specific Na⁺/K⁺ pump currents were nearly abolished, whereas α1 activity remained intact. This selective dysfunction was associated with a depolarized resting membrane potential, reduced input resistance, and diminished intrinsic excitability. Patient neurons generated fewer action potentials in response to depolarizing current steps, displayed altered firing patterns, and showed significantly decreased voltage-gated sodium current densities, while potassium conductance remained unaffected. Taken together, these results indicate that the ATP1A3 E815K mutation disrupts intracellular sodium homeostasis and consequently modifies the excitability of human neurons. Overall, these findings provide mechanistic insight into the molecular pathophysiology underlying this AHC variant and thereby establish a patient-derived neuronal model which serves as a platform for future drug screening approaches and therapeutic investigation. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. ne1b93db1f870: The results in this article demonstrate that the central nervous system CNS plans trajectories in the vertical plane by minimizing a Generalized Dynamic Jerk GJerk cost function, which we have proposed as an advancement of the traditional Minimum Jerk cost function. While the traditional Jerk cost function generates smooth trajectories by minimizing the third derivative of joint angle over time, it neglects real dynamic constraints most notably the effect of gravity. According to our engineering interpretation, the arm functions as a constrained manipulator where gravity acts as a non-linear, state-dependent bias; thus, the asymmetry in velocity profiles is not an anomaly but an optimal adaptation to the gravitational field. Consequently, it predicts mathematically symmetrical upward and downward movements, even in contexts where gravitational forces play a decisive role. The proposed GJerk cost function extends the classical framework by incorporating position-dependent dynamic coefficients into the cost function, thereby embedding gravitational effects directly within the planning process. As a result, the generated movements are not only smooth in a mathematical sense but also physically and mechanically consistent with the actual torque and energy demands imposed by the musculoskeletal system. The GJerk cost function reduces angular change in high-gravitational-torque regions because it makes the joint configuration with the highest gravitational torque more expensive within the cost function, prompting the planner to choose a slower and more conservative movement. This does not physically dissipate energy, but it acts as a behavioral damping mechanism, similar to how humans naturally slow down when approaching a high load or potentially dangerous configuration. In this way, the GJerk cost function reduces abrupt changes in joint kinetic energy and prevents sudden jumps in acceleration, ultimately producing a smoother and more stable trajectory that aligns with both biomechanical reality and observed human behavior. Within this framework, upward movements become inherently more costly than downward ones, penalizing configurations that require large torques to counteract gravity. This induces a biomechanically meaningful asymmetry, ensuring the resulting trajectories reflect the body's true mechanical constraints rather than mere geometric smoothness. Our empirical results demonstrate that the GJerk cost function provides a more realistic and physiologically grounded account of motor planning in the vertical plane, linking smoothness optimization with genuine dynamic requirements and offering a closer approximation to biological motor behavior
n18a6532ec6ca: Trypanosoma vivax is a unicellular parasite spread by biting flies and an important livestock pathogen across sub-Saharan Africa and South America. Alongside its better known relative, T. brucei, it causes animal trypanosomosis. An accurate genome sequence is essential to functional genetics as well as the design of novel diagnostics, drugs and vaccines. However, the existing T. vivax genome sequence is fragmentary, making it difficult to examine genomic features such as the Variant Surface Glycoprotein (VSG) genes that are the basis for antigenic variation, a key phenotype that underpins immune evasion by African trypanosomes. Our aim was to produce a T. vivax genome sequence with improved contiguity to properly characterise the VSG genes. We present a new core genome assembly in 23 scaffolds, forming approximately 10 chromosomes. Many scaffolds are articulated with extensive sub-telomeric domains that, like T. brucei, contain VSG gene arrays but in T. vivax these are near-perfect repeats of intact genes. Using transcriptomic and proteomic analysis of VSG expression during bloodstream infection we show that the active VSG is expressed from a sub-telomeric array while other arrays are silent. We find no evidence for a VSG expression site at the telomeres or elsewhere. Therefore, although monoallelic expression and antigenic switching occur in T. vivax, the familiar regulatory mechanism of T. brucei does not exist in T. vivax. This improved T. vivax genome assembly demonstrates that T. brucei is a poor guide for T. vivax genetics generally and for regulation of antigenic variation specifically. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. nc753725af45e: Humans effortlessly shift their attention between objects and events in the environment. These attentional shifts modulate the representation of information in many regions of the cerebral cortex, including those that represent visual-semantic information. Based on recent evidence that the cerebellum also represents semantic information, we hypothesized that attention would also shift semantic representations in the cerebellum. To test this hypothesis, we used fMRI to measure brain activity while participants watched naturalistic movie clips and were instructed to attend to either people or vehicles. We used a voxelwise encoding model framework to recover visual-semantic representations in the cerebral cortex and cerebellum under the two conditions, and quantified the direction and magnitude of visual-semantic tuning shifts between conditions. Attention to different semantic categories had a large effect on visual-semantic tuning in the cerebellum. Representations in some regions shifted toward the attended category, and representations in other regions shifted away from the attended category. Within cerebellar regions that best represent visual-semantic information, the tuning shifts were most pronounced in Crus I and II and in lobule VI. Further, the magnitude of attentional tuning shifts was greater in the cerebellum than in the cerebral cortex, particularly for tuning shifts towards the attended category. These differences suggest that attentional modulation in the cerebellum is different than in the cerebral cortex and may not solely be driven by cerebral inputs. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n6a5846b3ec5d: Friedreich ataxia (FRDA) is an inherited multisystem disorder caused by a GAA repeat expansion in the FXN gene and consequent frataxin deficiency, causing progressive neurodegeneration and heart disease. Clinical studies have documented autonomic dysfunction in FRDA, including elevated resting heart rate, raised plasma catecholamines and a high burden of urinary, bowel and sexual symptoms. Consistent with this, autopsy studies show degeneration of the cardiac conduction system and its associated ganglia in FRDA. Whether these features are intrinsic to FRDA autonomic neurons has been untestable without a human cellular model. Here, a human model of FRDA autonomic neurons was established by differentiating induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) from individuals with FRDA and from their CRISPR/Cas9-corrected isogenic controls. FRDA autonomic neurons expressed canonical autonomic lineage markers and retained reduced FXN mRNA and frataxin protein levels. Electrophysiological analysis revealed pronounced hyperexcitability, with an approximately five-fold increase in spike number, shortened interspike intervals, and longer bursts. FRDA autonomic neurons also exhibited increased cell death, elevated mitochondrial reactive oxygen species, and a shift from networked to tubular mitochondrial morphology. Bulk RNA sequencing of all three isogenic pairs revealed loss of extracellular matrix programs and activation of stress response pathways. The top differentially expressed gene was MEG3, a maternally imprinted long noncoding RNA, which was consistently upregulated across all three isogenic pairs. MEG3 sits within the imprinted 14q32 DLK1-DIO3 locus, whose maternally expressed noncoding transcripts were co-ordinately de-repressed in FRDA autonomic neurons. Competitive gene-set testing of 43 imprinted genes across 20 domains showed this to be specific to 14q32: no other imprinted domain was co-ordinately altered. Together, these findings establish hyperexcitability of autonomic neurons as a cell autonomous consequence of frataxin deficiency, accompanied by mitochondrial dysfunction. This provides a cellular basis for the increased sympathetic tone observed in clinical studies. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n930677d555c4: Metagenomic databases hold vast quantities of unexplored genetic material that can seed tools for biotechnology and medicine, but discovery is limited by our ability to examine sequence data at scale. Here, we show that large language models (LLMs) in an autonomous harness can alleviate this bottleneck and surface novel molecular systems. We deployed Claude Code instances to survey reverse transcriptase (RT) loci across 1.9 billion protein clusters. Among the top candidates were array-associated RTs (ART), a novel family of jumbo-phage RTs coupled with an array of ~200-nucleotide units and a dedicated partner gene. Session transcripts show that Claude identified the ART family by directly examining its DNA sequences and recognizing the atypical repeats, a behavior attributable to specific Mythos 5 internal signals that respond to repeated DNA. ART arrays are highly expressed and appear as discrete units during Staphylococcus phage infection, suggesting an RT system directed by a repertoire of distinct RNAs. These findings indicate that LLMs can autonomously detect anomalies and drive analyses to initiate biological discoveries. ### Competing Interest Statement All authors are employees of Anthropic and may hold equity in the company. nc59d1bcf2200: Ayahuasca, used religiously for centuries by Amazonian Indigenous peoples and increasingly studied for its therapeutic potential, owes its psychoactivity to two plants: Psychotria viridis supplies N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT), whereas Banisteriopsis caapi supplies beta-carbolines that render DMT orally active. Here we show that the two plants have distinct genome histories: P. viridis is hexaploid (2n = 6x = 66), consistent with autopolyploidy, and B. caapi is diploid (2n = 2x = 20). CENH3-bound regions of both species are nonetheless enriched in CRM-type Ty3/Gypsy retrotransposons, with additional LINE elements and CRM-derived satellites in B. caapi. In P. viridis, a single multifunctional methyltransferase catalyzes both N-methylations of tryptamine to DMT. In B. caapi, beta-carboline biosynthesis combines dedicated enzymes with an acetaldehyde-dependent Pictet-Spengler cyclization that can proceed non-enzymatically, followed by enantioselective oxidation to harmaline. These resources link the ethnobotanical history of ayahuasca to its molecular basis, providing genomes of both source plants, the genetic structure of traditionally recognized cultivated varieties, and the enzymes behind the alkaloids long combined in this decoction. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
necfb9393fccc: Branched-chain amino acids (BCAA) have been implicated in diabetes and heart failure, leading to ongoing clinical trials with inhibitors of BCKDK, a key regulator of BCAA catabolism. We have previously shown that these inhibitors promote vasodilation and lower blood pressure, well-known cardioprotective effects, but how this occurs remained unclear. We show here, using explanted vessels, in vivo hemodynamics and telemetry, and genetically modified mice, that the vasodilatory effect of BCKDK inhibitors is direct, rapid, independent of nitric oxide, independent of BCAA catabolism, and most strikingly, independent of BCKDK itself. Instead, we demonstrate, using structural and biochemical studies, that BCKDK inhibitors directly antagonize the angiotensin II type I receptor (AT1R) and consequent angiotensin-mediated vasoconstriction. These data demonstrate a strong off-target effect of BCKDK inhibitors, independent of BCAA or BCKDK, which may explain their cardioprotective effects but also questions if this protection would be additive to existing AT1R blockers.
ne7eed58ebf9d: Clostridium botulinum Group I and Clostridium sporogenes are closely related genomic lineages for which historical toxin-based nomenclature can obscure species-level relationships. We developed BoNTax, a curated taxonomy-first framework that separates average nucleotide identity (ANI)-based species assignment from botulinum neurotoxin (BoNT) characterization while integrating assembly quality assessment, multilocus sequence typing (MLST), AMRFinderPlus-based detection of bont genes, other virulence-associated genes, and antimicrobial resistance genes into standardized outputs. Analysis of 966 genomes informed genome-size criteria and the selection of 46 representative references comprising 22 C. botulinum Group I and 24 C. sporogenes genomes. Pairwise ANI resolved these references into two distinct species clusters: within-species ANI values were >95%, whereas between-species values were <95%, supporting a 95% species-level assignment threshold. BoNTax was implemented in GalaxyTrakr as complementary FASTQ- and FASTA-input workflows that converge on a common downstream analysis. The workflow completed analysis of all 42 validation genomes. Among the 32 genomes with a reported taxonomic identity, 29 assignments were concordant and three prompted taxonomic re-evaluations. For the ten genomes reported as taxonomically unknown, BoNTax provided ANI-based assignments. Of the three discordances, BT-22100019 was assigned to C. sporogenes rather than the reported C. botulinum Group I, whereas R1125/03 and R1135/03 showed 99.96% ANI to C. caseinilyticum DSM 46279, supporting their identification as C. caseinilyticum. MLST assignments were concordant for genomes with established profiles except PNUSAB000061, for which ST183 was not assigned by the MLST database version used in this analysis. BoNT type and subtype detection was fully concordant across toxigenic genomes, including bivalent strains. Thirty-one genomes met the predefined assembly-size QC criterion, whereas 11 received QC warnings, including all eight datasets representing four known mixed cultures. BoNTax therefore provides a reproducible genomic framework for resolving closely related clostridial lineages, identifying taxonomic annotations requiring re-evaluation, and reporting clinically relevant toxin information without conflating toxin genotype with species identity.
n67aff92d3001: Objective. Frontal-midline theta (FM-theta; 4-8 Hz) oscillations are thought to support cognition. Brief trains of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) can probe these oscillations with high temporal precision but have rarely changed theta power. One possible reason is that prior studies ignored the instantaneous phase of the oscillation, which strongly shapes the cortical response to TMS. We tested whether brief TMS trains triggered at specific FM-theta phases in real time directionally modulate post-train FM-theta power. Approach. Six healthy adults received TMS over dorsomedial prefrontal cortex (Fz) with concurrent electroencephalography during a whole-report working memory task. A beamformer and real-time phase-estimation pipeline triggered four-pulse 6 Hz trains (110% of resting motor threshold) at FM-theta peaks (0 degrees) or troughs (180 degrees), randomized trial by trial. Post-train spectral power was decomposed into total, induced (non-phase-locked) and evoked (phase-locked) components. Main results. Trough-triggered trains transiently increased post-train FM-theta power relative to peak-triggered trains; task performance did not differ. Cluster-based permutation tests showed trough−peak differences in total (4.6-7.1 Hz) and induced (5.0-7.8 Hz) power ~50-440 ms after the train, suggesting amplification of the oscillation . No evoked effect was detected. The total-power effect was robust at the subject level (Cohen's dz = 1.32, p = 0.023). Within-train theta power did not differ between conditions, suggesting a cortical origin. Significance. To our knowledge, this is the first study to lock brief rhythmic TMS trains to the real-time phase of an ongoing oscillation, and to show phase-dependent modulation of FM-theta power after individual trains on timescales relevant to behavior. Open-loop brief-train protocols may have missed such effects by mixing faciliatory and suppressive phases. Phase-locked brief trains offer a precise tool for testing the causal role of oscillations in cognition. ### Competing Interest Statement AD is employed by Starfish Neuroscience, who made a philanthropic donation to JDM. n353a7b6e4f0e: While the immune reset induced by CD19 CAR T therapies has shown striking promise in systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), the nature and duration of benefit mediated by B cell depletion remains unclear. Loss of tolerance in SLE is driven by extrafollicular and germinal center interactions between dendritic cells and self-reactive T and B cells. We hypothesized that CD19 CAR-engineered regulatory T cells (CAR19 EngTreg), capable of suppressing multiple autoimmune effector cell types, might promote long-term tolerance without producing high-levels of inflammatory mediators. To generate CAR19 EngTreg, we combined CD19 CAR delivery with homology directed repair at the FOXP3 locus to drive constitutive, stable FOXP3 expression in CD4 T cells. CAR19 EngTreg expressed canonical Treg markers; exhibited minimal inflammatory cytokine production; and blocked human B cell differentiation into antibody secreting plasma cells. In humanized mouse models, transfer of CAR19 EngTreg led to a reduction in B cell numbers with low inflammatory cytokine production relative to CD19 CAR Teff, and reduced tissue inflammation. In a short-term, in vivo imiquimod-induced inflammatory model, murine CAR19 EngTreg reduced skin pathology, spleen size, and inflammatory cytokines. Finally, in two distinct mouse models of lupus, CAR19 EngTreg persisted for >4 months leading to reduced autoimmune T and B effector populations, sustained reduction in multiple autoantibodies and improved renal function and histopathology. Thus, CAR19 EngTreg may offer a promising and durable therapeutic avenue for B cell-mediated autoimmune disorders capable of long-term regulation of both autoreactive B and T cells. ### Competing Interest Statement VDN, MH, JM, MM, PZ, AB, CM, CP, TC, ADRE, and TW are current or former employees of GentiBio. na2f1ac2b6c41: Functionally linking enhancers to gene promoters at high resolution often entails analysis of 3C datasets, including viewpoint-based methods such as Capture-(Hi)C. Quantitative comparison across samples and experiments, together with visualization and integration of promoter interactions with other datasets are of critical importance. While existing statistical tools identify significant interactions and quantify underlying signal, systematically comparing the shape and extent of this signal across large sets of intervals remains challenging. Moreover, experimental artefacts, such as inefficient crosslinking, can affect downstream interpretation, but are difficult to detect systematically. Here we introduce PostChicago, an R/Bioconductor package that fills this gap. Building upon the widely used interaction-calling package Chicago, PostChicago provides a complete workflow for quality control, visualization, integration and quantitative analysis of promoter interactions between multiple samples, including annotation and quantification of genomic regions based on external datasets. PostChicago extends visual quantitative comparisons beyond individual viewpoints by computing normalized metaprofiles around large sets of intervals that visualize the distribution of interaction signal, enabling comparison between narrow and broad interaction patterns. We further demonstrate how PostChicago can identify experimental crosslinking artefacts. Together, PostChicago enables integrative, shape-sensitive analysis and quality control of promoter Capture-(Hi)C datasets at a scale that would otherwise require extensive custom scripting.
n83523cc7b7ef: Identifying which gene drives a desired cell-state transition is a foundational inverse problem in target discovery and cell-state engineering, yet far less developed than forward prediction. We show that prevailing benchmarks inflate performance through two artefacts: training leakage, where test-perturbation cells are seen during fitting, and evaluation leakage, where the perturbed gene's own expression change exposes the answer. Here, we introduce Cause-excluded Effect Evaluation (CEE), a framework that separates train and test perturbation targets, removes target-gene self-effects from expression profiles and scores candidates in downstream response space. With CEE, we find that simple structure-based methods consistently outperform complex deep learning models across 16 single-cell perturbation datasets, revealing that the recoverable signal is governed by low-rank and additive structure in perturbation responses rather than by model complexity. Our work disentangles evaluation artefacts from genuine predictive capacity and offers a design principle for developing perturbation target identification methods. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n2da04697fcbe: A major challenge in precision medicine is to understand the cellular origin of disease-causing genetic alterations. One prominent example is the Negr1 locus, where common non-coding variants are associated with an unusually broad range of human traits and conditions, including body mass index (BMI), major depression, schizophrenia, autism-spectrum conditions and anorexia. Yet, no coding loss-of-function allele has been established as causal. These observations suggest that distinct Negr1-expressing cell populations underlie distinct traits. However, this hypothesis is difficult to test in tractable experimental systems without first determining where this gene may act. To overcome this limitation, we generated a knock-in reporter at the zebrafish Negr1 locus and combined single-cell transcriptomics with whole-brain registration and single-neuron projection mapping. We found that Negr1 is expressed in a graded manner across neuronal classes of the brain and retina, radial glia and astrocyte-like cells, and most consistently in oligodendrocyte progenitor cells. Projection mapping suggests three conserved hubs formed by olfactory bulb projection neurons, tectal periventricular projection neurons and cerebellar eurydendroid cells. Our findings are consistent with the idea that Negr1 pleiotropy arises from dose perturbation of a rather broadly expressed gene. More generally, this integrative approach to produce granular multimodal datasets should enable high-resolution etiological studies in models of human disease. ### Competing Interest Statement H.L-S. is a scientific advisor for the biotechnology company Sensorion. nce778c0cc0fd: Many animals use the Earth's magnetic field to orient and navigate over long distances, yet the sensory mechanism that underlies this ability remains unresolved. A central question is whether the compass depends on light: a cryptochrome-based radical-pair mechanism, best characterised in birds, requires a photon to generate the magnetically sensitive species, whereas magnetic particle-based and inductive mechanisms do not. In mammals, which lack the light-sensitive cryptochromes that the avian model requires, this question is unresolved. Here we tested whether migratory bats, Pipistrellus nathusii, require light for migratory orientation, studying wild migrants at a major flyway under laboratory-controlled light conditions, including verified total darkness. Bats were acclimated to starlight-level illumination or to total darkness before release into a circular arena in which take-off direction was recorded, and take-off latency was taken in every trial as a control for behavioural state. Bats released under starlight-level illumination, and bats released in total darkness after starlight acclimation, both oriented in the south-westerly direction typical of free-flying bats at this flyway; their mean headings lay 11 degrees apart and did not differ in direction, in angular concentration, or in take-off latency. Bats released in total darkness after prolonged darkness produced the same mean heading but did not reach significance under a Rayleigh test, and did not differ from either other group. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that a migratory mammal expresses its seasonally appropriate migratory heading in total darkness. Bats orienting in darkness took off five to eight minutes after their last photon exposure, seven to eight orders of magnitude beyond the microsecond lifetime of the only cryptochrome radical pair demonstrated to exist and to be magnetically sensitive. Because a compass reading is informative only at the moment of the directional decision, a signal generated before a bat entered darkness could not encode its heading at take-off; the magnetically sensitive species must therefore form without photons. The radical pairs capable of doing so have not been shown to exist, even in vitro. A migratory mammal thus expresses its seasonal heading without concurrent light, in a lineage lacking the photoreceptor on which the light-dependent compass in birds relies. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. nb627d6f0f48f: Introduction: Early Alzheimer's disease (AD) staging remains challenging because clinical categories and global amyloid PET measures provide only coarse characterization of disease progression. Cognitive analyses were replicated in A4+LEARN. Results: The staging score better preserved longitudinal visit order than existing amyloid staging approaches. During early disease stages, it captured regional amyloid variation despite relatively stable global amyloid burden. Among participants with similar baseline global amyloid burden, higher staging scores were associated with faster subsequent memory decline in both ADNI and A4+LEARN. Discussion: A continuous amyloid staging score complements global amyloid burden for early AD staging and cognitive risk stratification. n60cf08b54842: Metabolic repertoires are continually remodeled by gene acquisition and loss, but how these contrasting processes jointly generate phenotypic diversity within bacterial species complexes remains poorly understood. Although this classification has been used for over half a century, the genetic determinants and evolutionary origins of these phenotypes have not been systematically resolved. Comparative phylogenomics revealed fundamentally different evolutionary histories of these loci. An ancestral smoEFGK system was lost early in RSSC evolution and subsequently reacquired by the ancestor of phylotype I through horizontal transfer from a Burkholderia-related lineage, whereas vertically inherited FADGDH underwent recurrent, independent losses across multiple RSSC lineages. Extending the analysis to 1,082 RSSC strains further showed that disaccharide-utilization capacity was significantly depleted among monocot-associated strains after accounting for phylogenetic relatedness and geographic origin. n9b80302516ad: Aim To investigate how repeated historical connections between continental islands and the mainland have shaped the phylogeographic structure and genetic diversity of populations, using the widespread water strider Aquarius paludum as a model. Bayesian phylogenetic analyses identified two major mitochondrial haplogroups (A and B) that frequently co-occurred across the Japanese archipelago. Haplogroup A, which is rare on the Eurasian continent, occurred at high frequency in Japan and showed pronounced isolation by distance, whereas haplogroup B showed only weak but significant isolation by distance and was significantly more frequent in populations closer to the coast. n3bfe8dfa4d20: Nasu-Hakola disease (NHD), a dementia with about 200 cases worldwide, is caused by loss-of-function mutation of TYROBP, encoding DAP12, or its receptor TREM2. We profiled prefrontal cortex and hippocampus from an NHD donor and control by single-nucleus RNA sequencing and mapped the glial changes in situ by spatial transcriptomics. NHD microglia adopted a CIITA-driven, MHC class II-high antigen-presenting state with complement, iron and glycolytic programs and Fc receptors but not the TREM2-dependent lipid program. Astrocytes became pan-reactive and lost metallothionein expression, oligodendrocytes lost mature cells and cholesterol synthesis, and excitatory neurons lost presynaptic and activity programs, consistently between regions and across a published cohort. n8cad2ad8e199: Spatial transcriptomics increasingly generates multi-slice atlases spanning developmental, regenerative, and disease-associated states. Here we introduce DeSPA, a statistical framework that models gene-specific spatial variation within each slice using a linear mixed model, tests for cross-state remodeling by aggregating evidence across replicate slices, and organizes identified genes into interpretable spatial co-expression modules that reveal coordinated spatial programs. Simulations show that DeSPA achieves high power while controlling the false discovery rate under inter-slice heterogeneity. In mouse embryogenesis, it recovers programs linked to extracellular matrix organization, muscle formation, neural development, and erythrocyte development. In diabetic testis, it reveals disruption of a late-spermatid spatial program consistent with known spermatogenic dysfunction, while maintaining stable gene rankings under coordinate rotation. In axolotl brain, regeneration preserves a developmental-like biosynthetic backbone but reorganizes it into regeneration-specific modules. Across two mouse intracerebral hemorrhage models, DeSPA resolves a conserved spatial injury program alongside model-specific synaptic and tissue-response programs. Together, these findings establish DeSPA as a scalable and interpretable framework for detecting spatial pattern remodeling and resolving coordinated spatial programs across diverse biological states. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
n764a6c463d3f: Early-life adversity and abnormal myelination are implicated in psychiatric disorders, but how developmental myelination influences adult social cognition remains unclear. Spatial transcriptomics revealed coupling between myelin-related genes and parvalbumin (PV) interneuron markers in the healthy mPFC, which was disrupted by developmental hypomyelination. naaf8090947d0: The external parabrachial nucleus (elPBN) contributes to diverse behaviors, including pain and stress. nd8ba3d5ca272: Human fetal haematopoiesis requires developmental potential to be encoded before lineage identity becomes transcriptionally apparent, but whether three-dimensional genome architecture provides such information is unknown. Unexpectedly, B-lineage and erythroid differentiation followed opposing architectural trajectories, with progressive loss and gain of chromatin connectivity, respectively. Deletion of a T21-sensitive EBF1 loop anchor reproduced the CLP-to-B-progenitor bottleneck observed in T21. These findings establish 3D genome architecture as an organizing layer of human fetal haematopoiesis that links developmental potential with lineage-specific vulnerability to genomic perturbation.
ndcc699899ca9: Neuroimaging studies have identified a specialised social brain network that supports emotion recognition and social cognition. This network performs a range of functions that include facial expression recognition and inferring the mental states of others. To investigate how transient disruption of the right IFG affects the wider social brain we combined transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) with functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI). Participants (n=20) were scanned across two sessions while performing a delayed match-to-sample emotion recognition task in which happy or fearful expressions were preceded by a congruent or incongruent word cue. Prior to each scan, thetaburst TMS was delivered over the right IFG or over the vertex control site (session order was balanced across participants). A group whole-brain analysis revealed that TMS to the IFG increased neural activity in multiple regions of the social brain network. These included the bilateral temporal pole, precuneus and medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC). This pattern of results shows that the disruption of top-down control mechanisms localised in the IFG alters the neural processing in remote nodes of the social brain network. Our findings are discussed within the wider context of how we recognise and understand the emotions of other people.
n68f113995f79: Developmental dyscalculia is a learning disorder characterized by marked difficulties in numerical cognition, yet its cognitive and neural underpinnings remain debated. Here, we test both accounts in 33 adolescents and young adults with dyscalculia and 33 age- and gender-matched controls (15-23 years) who performed a sequential numerosity comparison task during fMRI. Joint computational modeling of choices and response times allowed us to dissociate perceptual and memory noise from decision variables governing the speed-accuracy tradeoff, while complementary neuroimaging analyses characterized neural number representations and their network embedding. Specifically, we quantified the precision of parietal numerosity tuning with numerical population receptive field (nPRF) modeling and derived individualized functional network maps of the same region using community detection algorithms applied to connectivity patterns. Dyscalculic participants showed greater perceptual and memory noise but also a more cautious response criterion, trading speed for accuracy to compensate for representational imprecision. Neurally, the numerosity model explained less variance in parietal cortex, suggesting less precise numerical representations, and individualized network maps assigned less of this cortex to the dorsal attention network and more to a visual network. Rather than supporting a dichotomy between the two accounts, our findings suggest that dyscalculia reflects both less precise numerical representations in parietal cortex and an altered allocation of this cortex to distributed functional systems. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
n2d85d99de292: Prenatal stress influences brain development; however, its long-term, region-specific effects on brain aging in males and females remain insufficiently characterized. These outcomes corresponded with accelerated fronto-striatal decline, likely mediated by insulin resistance and increased rigidity of medial prefrontal cortex structures due to diminished local estrogenic activity. In contrast, middle-aged stressed females displayed hypoactivity and reduced anxiety, later developing anhedonia in old age while maintaining hippocampus-dependent memory. In females, this pattern supports a model in which a neuroestrogen - and growth factor-dependent feedback loop transiently preserves hippocampal plasticity but compromises dopaminergic function in reward circuits. This balance may deteriorate with reproductive senescence. Both sexes retained cognitive flexibility, indicating domain-specific rather than global cognitive impairment. These findings demonstrate that excessive prenatal glucocorticoid exposure and unpredictable postnatal care produce a combined hormonal and metabolic insult, resulting in sexually divergent trajectories of brain aging. The results underscore the necessity of incorporating sex as a biological variable in fetal programming research across the lifespan. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. nce1e5c44d7f6: Fluctuating asymmetry (FA) is widely used as a proxy for developmental instability, although reduced rather than increased FA, has occasionally been reported under particularly challenging conditions, possibly because environmental filtering removes less developmentally stable individuals. Here, we investigated temporal variation in wing shape asymmetry in males of Drosophila sturtevanti collected in 2022, 2024, and 2026 at the same sampling site, an urban Atlantic Forest fragment. Sampling in 2022 and 2026 were completed during single field expeditions in early April, whereas in 2024 repeated collections were required until mid-May because of markedly low capture success. We therefore examined whether this difference was associated with unusual environmental conditions and whether FA was higher in 2024, as expected under greater developmental perturbation. Daily temperature and relative humidity were examined from early March onward, encompassing approximately one month before adult emergence. The 2024 sampling period was warmer and drier than the corresponding periods in 2022 and 2026 and coincided with the final phase of the strong 2023-2024 El Ni&ntildeo event. Contrary to our prediction, FA was significantly lower in 2024. The magnitude of directional asymmetry remained similar among years, although the spatial pattern of the DA vector differed between 2024 and 2026. nce443b13e779: Motivation: Optimum contribution selection (OCS) maximizes genetic gain under a constraint on relatedness. Genomic relationship matrices are dense, so the quadratic term costs O(n^3) operations, and existing OCS software assumes pedigree sparsity. Results: We replace the relationship matrix by its leading eigenpairs, computed by randomized SVD, and solve OCS in factorized form. On Norway spruce population (n=5,525), ranks 10--30 kept the exact objective within 1% of the optimum at 110--330-fold speedups; on the QTL-MAS 2010 (n=3,226), ranks up to 100 were needed (24-211 fold). The required rank rises as the diversity constraint loosens. Gain alone is a misleading accuracy check, since coancestry exceeded the optimum by up to 28%, so we choose the rank on the exact objective, which can be checked without a dense solve. The speedup comes from computing only the leading eigenpairs. We extend the factorization to robust OCS (18-fold). Availability and implementation: Julia implementation, and examples are available at https://github.com/jonhar97/fastocs under the MIT license (archived at Zenodo, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23214804). ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. na7723f7e65bc: Gene duplication is a major driver of genomic innovation, but whether paralog accumulation scales uniformly with increasing genome size across the domain Archaea remains unclear. Protein family expansions were classified as recent (90% sequence identity), intermediate (70%), or old (40%) duplications based on sequence-identity thresholds within each family. The findings show that gene duplication content is decoupled from overall proteome size at high sequence-identity levels, indicating that recent paralog retention does not correlate with proteome expansion. Archaeal lineages exhibit contrasting gene duplication profiles. All 1,829 genomes contained paralogs at the 40% sequence identity threshold, indicating the widespread presence of ancient or divergent duplication events. In contrast, paralogs detected at the 90% identity threshold, showed substantial variation across lineages. Their proportion reached up to 16.6% in groups such as Halobacteria, whereas only 74 genomes (4.04%) completely lacked paralogs at this threshold. Highly duplicated families are enriched for membrane transport systems (ABC/MFS), central metabolic enzymes (e.g., acetyl-CoA synthetase), a high proportion of uncharacterized functions, and mobile elements, predominantly transposases. Notably, we identified 314 transposase protein families in Archaea, distributed in 161 unique families in Archaea and 153 families shared with Bacteria, suggesting mechanisms of interdomain gene transfer. Overall, paralog accumulation in Archaea is a lineage-specific phenomenon shaped by targeted functional duplications and mobile element activity, rather than a simple consequence of proteome growth. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n6b9b3f0c7d2f: Fragile X syndrome (FXS) features sensory, social, and cognitive dysfunction, but how fragile X messenger ribonucleoprotein 1 (FMR1) deficiency disrupts sensory corticostriatal circuitry and whether distinct FMR1 perturbations converge on shared cellular mechanisms remain incompletely defined. Moreover, mt-EcGAPR-based Mitochondrial OptoEnergetic Activation (Mito-OptoEA) enhanced mitochondrial energetic state in S1 and improved novel-location recognition and sociability in both Fmr1-KO and I234T models. Together, these findings define a sensory corticostriatal circuit-metabolic framework for FXS in which S1-DMS circuit dysfunction and convergent mitochondrial energetic abnormalities contribute to FMR1-related social and cognitive phenotypes. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n90c2c62b16f8: Metaproteomics analyses require protein sequence databases, yet the microbial proteins present in complex communities are not known in advance. Searching reference catalogs containing hundreds of millions of candidate sequences reduces identification sensitivity, while generating sample-specific databases through metagenomic sequencing adds time and cost. In a defined eight-member community, FastaLake approached reference-search peptide yields without knowing its members. Using public sequence catalogs, FastaLake identified about as many peptides as matched metagenomic databases in two stool cohorts and 20-35% more in intestinal fluid at the same nominal 1% peptide false discovery rate. The resulting proteomes reveal personal functional profiles that persist across intestinal regions despite differences in leading species between intestinal fluid and stool. DNA, RNA and protein profiles agreed on broad differences between patients but only weakly on individual functions. All 726 acquisition-specific databases were smaller than the human reference proteome. Compact databases allowed non-specific searches of all 347 CapScan acquisitions, revealing histidine enrichment at peptide C termini in intestinal fluid. FastaLake enables metaproteomics analysis without matched metagenomic sequencing by constructing search databases from sequence resources and de novo peptide sequencing.
nd8d868ca90d2: Protein inverse folding, which infers compatible amino acid sequences from a given backbone structure, is central to rational protein design. Current methods rely largely on sequence recovery rate as the evaluation metric, emphasizing structural compatibility but seldom addressing function. Yet functional activity depends on the proper network of non-covalent interactions-protein-ligand contacts being a prime example. We argue that function-oriented protein design is governed by three complementary constraints: structural, interaction, and evolutionary, none of which are handled in a unified manner by existing pretrained models. To bridge this gap, we introduce zPolaron, a graph neural network built on protein-ligand complexes for functional protein design. zPolaron represents residues and ligand atoms as a heterogeneous graph and jointly encodes structural, interaction, and evolutionary information by fusing physical-interaction-enhanced graph representations with ESM-2 embeddings. Across multiple fitness prediction benchmarks, zPolaron outperforms all baselines, with gains evident across structural, interaction, and evolutionary dimensions. Wet-lab experiments further confirm its utility in functional enzyme screening and design: the optimized CalA6-D205A-S160G mutant achieves a 17.84-fold improvement in activity, while the CalB-I121M mutant yields a 1.91-fold increase. Together, these results show that integrating interaction and evolutionary information fills the missing puzzle of inverse folding, enhancing protein fitness prediction beyond structural compatibility. zPolaron is available at https://github.com/zelixirSH/zPolaron.
n93405c0b19af: Background: Surveillance tells laboratories which antimicrobial resistance genes are circulating now, but not which will change next. We built a model that forecasts, for each resistance gene and year, whether the following year brings a previously unseen allele (sequence variant), called emergence, or a change in the most common allele, called turnover. We tested it separately in Klebsiella pneumoniae and Acinetobacter baumannii. Results: We used genomes annotated with AMRFinderPlus: 2,385 gene-years across 331 genes for K.pneumoniae and 1,059 across 216 for A. baumannii. To remove the effect of sequencing effort, each gene-year was sampled to 10 records and the analysis repeated 25 times. Models were trained on earlier years and tested on later ones, and on genes held out of training. On later years every model ranked genes by risk better than simple baselines in both organisms, and results for held-out genes were close. In K.pneumoniae, turnover was predicted better than emergence (best area under the ROC curve, AUROC, 0.909 versus 0.819). In A. baumannii the order reversed (emergence 0.789, turnover 0.722). The two events also relied on different features. Emergence depended mainly on how many alleles a gene had already accumulated, in both organisms. Turnover in K. pneumoniae depended mainly on how dominant the leading allele already was, and a stability index added a small gain. In A. baumannii it was spread across many weaker features. There, 56% of changes in the leading allele involved only alleles already seen, against 23% in K. pneumoniae, which may make them harder to predict. Conclusions: Changes in resistance genes can be forecast a year ahead from routine genomic surveillance data, including for genes the model has not seen. How well it works, and what it depends on, differs between organisms, so models should be built and validated for each organism, not assumed to transfer. Such models could help laboratories decide which resistance genes to monitor most closely. Keywords: antimicrobial resistance; genomic surveillance; forecasting; machine learning; allele dynamics; Klebsiella pneumoniae; Acinetobacter baumannii ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
n78e4bd363a58: Open genomic repositories have become critical infrastructure for pathogen surveillance, variant tracking, outbreak reconstruction, and public health decision making. However, many of these repositories were designed to support rapid scientific data sharing rather than adversarial verification, creating potential security gaps. This paper introduces Advanced Persistent Biological Threats (APBTs), as a framework for understanding how malicious cyber biological actors can gradually disrupt genomic surveillance without entering a laboratory or releasing a biological agent. Instead of altering biological material, an attacker targets the sequence data, metadata, reference datasets, and analytical models used by surveillance systems. We present, to our knowledge, the first integrated multilayer taxonomy of APBTs, structured around a four phase lifecycle, and investigate whether the metadata weaknesses identified by this framework are present in an operational genomic repository. To assess this, we audited 100,000 SARS-CoV-2 BioSample records obtained from the NCBI. A framework of 23 checks was applied across five metadata layers: temporal, geographic, host and specimen, provenance, and technical metadata. Every record triggered at least one APBT relevant metadata vulnerability indicator, with a mean of 7.34 indicators per record (SD = 1.34). Overall, 97.3% of records were classified in the High or Critical severity categories. Every record also contained at least one indicator in both the provenance and technical metadata layers. These results largely reflect the optional status of several fields in the current BioSample submission model rather than isolated errors by individual data contributors. Temporal and geographic information was comparatively complete, while fields needed for provenance reconstruction, chain of custody assessment, technical validation, and analytical interpretation were frequently missing. These findings do not indicate deliberate manipulation. However, the structural incompleteness of BioSample metadata creates vulnerabilities that an adversary can exploit to introduce poisoned, misleading, or weakly traceable metadata into genomic repositories. As a result, maliciously altered metadata can appear plausible, remain undetected, and influence downstream genomic analysis and surveillance. The findings therefore show that widely used pathogen genomic repositories already contain structural weaknesses that can support metadata poisoning as part of an APBT operation. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n63fcf49ccf03: Palm oil is the worlds leading vegetable oil, with production continuing to expand, particularly across Southeast Asia. Within established plantations, conserving and restoring riparian margins can reduce erosion, improve connectivity, and support biodiversity. Simultaneously, climate change is increasing thermal stress within tropical agricultural landscapes, raising the potential importance of riparian buffers as microclimatic refugia, although this has not previously been evaluated. The Riparian Ecosystem Restoration in Tropical Agriculture (RERTA) Project is a long-term Before-After Control-Impact experiment established within oil palm plantations in Riau, Indonesia, to evaluate alternative riparian restoration strategies following plantation replanting. Treatments included passive restoration (retaining mature oil palms and allowing natural regeneration), active restoration (enrichment planting with six native tree species), and a control (replanting immature oil palms to the river edge). Six years after restoration, we assessed vegetation structure using terrestrial laser scanning and thermal stability using temperature loggers and thermal imaging. We also evaluated the long-term temperature buffering capacity of each treatment under current and projected climates using CHELSA climate data and downscaled outputs from multiple General Circulation Models under Shared Socioeconomic Pathway scenarios for 2045 and 2085. Active restoration produced greater structural complexity, a more closed canopy, and cooler, more thermally stable conditions than passive restoration and control treatments. Restored margins also contained significantly more cool surface microhabitats, reducing thermal extremes under both current and future climate scenarios. Our findings demonstrate that active restoration of riparian margins can enhance thermal buffering and create microclimatic refugia for biodiversity within tropical oil palm landscapes. As agricultural intensification and climate change continue to reshape tropical ecosystems, restoring structurally complex riparian vegetation will be critical for sustaining biodiversity and the ecosystem services upon which agricultural production depends. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. John Stanley Gardiner - SBS University Fund DTP Studentship
n4d8dcd4c975f: Perceptual decisions engage distributed brain networks, yet how decision-related signals are organized across and within brain areas remains unclear. Mesoscale functional domains are established in visual cortex, but whether spatially distinct domains organize perceptual decisions across the brain is unknown. Here we used 7-T functional MRI at 1-mm isotropic resolution in two awake macaques performing a contrast-discrimination task to map brain-wide activity during sensation, decision formation and saccadic report. Voxel timecourses separated into three groups with distinct temporal profiles, associated with sensory, decision-related and action-related activity. Their spatial distributions formed a broad progression from visual cortex to parietal, prefrontal and motor regions, while revealing distinct response domains within these regions. Choice-related signals were distributed across sensory, associative, and motor systems before movement, including in visual cortex responses to physically identical stimuli that differed according to the animal's eventual choice. Moreover, within the intraparietal sulcus and other regions, mesoscale domains preferentially responsive to near-threshold conditions carried choice information under uncertainty, whereas domains responsive to high-contrast conditions carried choice information when evidence was strong. These findings reveal that perceptual decisions are organized across the brain through spatially differentiated mesoscale networks whose activity varies with task phase and sensory certainty. This spatial organization provides a framework for investigating how distributed neural signals support flexible choice. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n2a6177c85ac4: Reliable classification of transposable elements (TEs) is important for genome annotation and evolutionary analysis, yet remains challenging: TE families differ widely across taxa, reference databases label them inconsistently, and many TEs are represented only by degraded copies. We introduce GLARE (Genomic Language model for Automated Repetitive Element classification), a TE classifier built by fine-tuning a genomic language model on harmonized PanTEon and Repbase reference data to predict TE superfamily across 32 superfamilies in 11 orders. Among the genomic language models compared, Nucleotide Transformer v3 provided the strongest representation. Built on this backbone, GLARE exceeded all nine classifiers in the PanTEon benchmark, reaching 0.966 weighted superfamily F1 on its 30-superfamily task. GLARE also showed stronger generalization to clades absent from training, consistently exceeding state-of-the-art classifiers on holdouts spanning three taxonomic ranks: the order Poales, the phylum Arthropoda, and the kingdom Fungi. Training on both PanTEon and Repbase reduced the performance drop seen when a single-source model was applied to the other database. Under simulated sequence decay, GLARE was the most robust classifier tested, and it performed best on independently curated degraded libraries. These findings show that genomic language models fine-tuned on harmonized multi-source references can classify TEs robustly under the taxonomic, database, and sequence-quality shifts that matter in practice. GLARE is available at https://code.jgi.doe.gov/NHaas/glare. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. United States Department of Energy, DE-AC02-05CH11231
n8727532a6125: Classical multilocus theory predicts that selection acting on combinations of loci can maintain non-random associations among allelic states, causing selection to act on multilocus genotypes rather than individual alleles. Across eukaryotic species, pangenome studies have documented thousands of genes that vary in functional status between individuals, yet this variation is analyzed as if each gene evolves independently. Here we test for non-random association within the dispensable pangenome across 1,012 natural genotypes of Arabidopsis thaliana to better understand the structure and evolution of eukaryotic pangenomes. Genome-wide pairwise association testing of loss-of-function alleles across genotypes identified 150,033 significantly covarying gene pairs among 5,679 unique genes after controlling for kinship and population structure. Most associations were between genes on different chromosomes, and covarying gene pairs showed greater co-expression and functional similarity than expected by chance. Network analysis revealed a non-random higher-order architecture comprising stable functional communities with distinct biological functions and structured connectivity among communities. The enriched functions and connectivity of communities revealed a tight coupling of modules involving plant immunity, environmental response, and specialized metabolism, highlighting how these systems integrate and evolve in response to dynamic ecological pressures. Taken together, these results show that the dispensable genome has a complex higher-order structure driven by functionally interacting genes, and that variation in gene content provides a population-scale resource for investigating the organization and evolution of biological systems. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Division of Integrative Organismal Systems, 2208944
nc2e10b4919a8: Environmental change is a major driver of adaptation, yet most evolutionary studies assume that genetic effects remain constant across environments. Recent biobank-scale studies have identified widespread gene-environment interactions (GxE), but their contribution to recent human evolution remains unclear. Here, we combined genome-wide GxE maps with allele-frequency trajectories spanning the last ~10,000 years to test whether environmentally responsive variants contributed to recent human adaptation. Among 45 independent loci, three showed significant signatures of directional selection. These loci, associated with urate, LDL-C and cholesterol levels, showed parallel frequency increases and overlapping acceleration points around 4,700-7,200 years ago. Selection-associated GxE loci were enriched for urate-related variants and for interactions involving meat and cheese consumption. Diet-associated variants showed a consistent interaction direction across loci. Notably, across candidate traits, GxE variants were enriched among significant GWAS loci with selection signatures. Furthermore, analyses across worldwide populations revealed broadly shared derived allele frequency increases and comparable temporal patterns. Taken together, our results suggest that gene-environment interactions present an important and previously underappreciated component of recent human evolution. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n7b9961d43042: We present draft genome assemblies for two poneroid ant species with distinctive life history traits: Platythyrea mocquerysi Emery, 1899 (Ponerinae) and Stigmatomma oregonense Wheeler, 1915 (Amblyoponinae). Platythyrea mocquerysi is a Malagasy ant in which larvae produce secretions from a ventral tubercle that are consumed by adults, representing an unusual form of larva-to-adult trophallaxis. Stigmatomma oregonense, a North American "dracula ant," feeds non-lethally on larval haemolymph. Using PacBio HiFi long-read sequencing, we assembled the P. mocquerysi genome (187 Mb, 307 scaffolds, N50 = 5.26 Mb, BUSCO 99.2% complete) and the S. oregonense genome (262 Mb, 1,189 scaffolds, N50 = 0.84 Mb, BUSCO 98.3% complete). These genomes encode 10,860 and 12,354 protein-coding genes, respectively. Repeat content is higher in S. oregonense than in P. mocquerysi, 54.3% against a lower bound of 15.7%. Most of the difference is in unclassified repeats, which we show to be diverged transposable elements. Comparative analysis with two additional poneroid genomes from closely related species reveals that genome size variation across poneroid ants is largely explained by transposable element dynamics, with notable expansions in several gene families including carboxylesterases, serine proteases, and lipid metabolism genes in Amblyoponinae. These genomes provide essential resources for investigating the molecular basis of unconventional brood management strategies in ants. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. n1f5eb182c682: Parasitoid wasps develop in or on other arthropods and have evolved a wide range of strategies for exploiting their hosts. Ascogaster reticulata is a solitary egg to larval endoparasitoid wasp belonging to the subfamily Cheloninae of Braconidae. We constructed a genome assembly using long-read sequence data. The assembled genome was 280.5 Mbp, consisting of 209 contigs. The N50 value and GC content ratio were 13.9 Mbp and 30.43%, respectively. The percentage of transposable elements and repetitive regions was 52.43%. The predicted number of genes is 27,261. Merqury revealed that the QV value and completeness of the genome were 61.79 and 99.3917%, respectively. BUSCO analysis detected approximately 99% of the core genes. These results suggest that the genome data were of sufficient quality for use as a reference genome. Therefore, these data can be utilized as a genomic resource for comparative studies within Braconidae and for future investigations into the biology and evolution of Cheloninae parasitoid wasps. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. ne5d3f0cdaa5f: Effective verbal communication requires individuals to align their communicative intentions through the precise use of utterances, yet how this is achieved in dynamic, open-ended communication remains unclear. Combining predictive deep language models (DLMs) with cognitive computational modeling, we tested a computational division of labor between context-sensitive global constraint on the utterance space and partner-sensitive local adjustment of selection priorities. We formalized local adjustment using an active inference inspired updating rule within a statistical-pragmatic hybrid model. Thirty dyads performed a dynamic, open-ended collaborative word-generation task during functional near infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) hyperscanning. Interlocutors converged in their lexical choices, and lexical alignment was best explained by a hybrid model integrating contextual selection priors with interaction-specific local adjustment among the models tested. This hybrid process formed a dynamic hypothesis landscape comprising a global semantic search region and local selection priorities. Critically, interaction did not simply reduce uncertainty: within individuals, the hypothesis space of global semantic search progressively narrowed while local uncertainty among plausible alternatives increased; between partners, both global hypothesis space and local selection became increasingly aligned, with alignment of local selection priorities most strongly predicting subsequent lexical alignment. The contribution of local adjustment was stronger during precise verbal communication than in the control tasks. Neural analyses further identified correlates of the local adjustment process: temporoparietal and anterior temporal regions supported partner-related inference and semantic prediction error, respectively, and their activity during thinking predicted subsequent inferior frontal activity associated with self-updating during speaking. The participant's own hypothesis landscape was also represented in the left inferior parietal-supramarginal cortex. The main findings generalized across language models and an independent Czech dataset. Together, these findings reveal that alignment in open-ended communication emerges from complementary statistical and pragmatic computations, providing a framework for understanding human and human-AI communication.
n57324194cdf1: The goat research community benefits from one of the most comprehensive livestock genome assemblies, ARS1. However, the rich diversity of goat breeds suggests that a single individual genome is not enough to represent the species full genomic content. Third-generation sequencing technologies have recently made it possible to generate very high quality assemblies that should enable to elucidate unique and/or complex phenotype determinisms depending on genetic structural variations. In the SeqOccin project, nine goat breeds were selected to represent French goat genetic diversity: Alpine, Boer, Creole, Fosses, Poitevine, Provencale, Pyreneenne, Rove and Saanen. High-molecular-weight DNA was extracted from blood samples and subjected to long read whole-genome sequencing. There reads were used to generate de novo assemblies and were aligned onto the public reference to call structural variants. PacBio HiFi and parental Illumina reads were used to assemble phased haplotypes of the Alpine breed. For the other breeds, PacBio raw (CLR) or ONT reads were generated. Our work demonstrates the feasibility of assembling genomes with a reasonable amount of data and appropriate software packages, delivering one high-quality assembly and 8 standard goat assemblies that pave the way for pangenome construction and structural variant functional studies. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. SeqOccIn
nc48284bab888: Borderline personality disorder (BPD) has traditionally been viewed as one of the most chronic psychiatric disorders. Although longitudinal studies have demonstrated promising rates of symptomatic remission, recovery and other clinical outcome measures often remain comparatively low. Qualitative research offers an important perspective on how individuals with BPD may extend a more representative view of improvement and change. We collected narratives from 41 participants with a self-reported diagnosis of BPD and analyzed them using thematic analysis. Its national, virtual recruitment approach enabled a relatively large qualitative sample diverse in gender identity, age, U.S. geographic region, treatment history, and current clinical severity, extending the range of perspectives represented in prior work. Three central themes were identified. The first, Differing attitudes toward language, reflected participants’experiences of recovery language as paradoxically both validating and stigmatizing. While individual language preferences varied, participants generally converged on a sharedunderstanding of what recovery meant to them. The second, Recovery as a dynamic and relational process, described recovery as nonlinear, effortful, and closely tied to interpersonal experiences. The third, Crossroads and uneven change over time, highlighted the role of personal agency, critical decision points in seeking treatment, and the persistence of internal distress even as behavioral symptoms improve. Findings from this study both replicate and extend existing qualitative research by discussing how individuals with BPD understand recovery in ways that may not be captured by traditional clinical outcome measures. These results emphasize the importance of incorporating lived-experience perspectives when defining recovery and setting treatment goals.
ndaf72b70cc08: Background: Patient-facing AI intake chatbots can enter clinical use without regulatory review, so their errors may first surface with actual patients. Objective: To develop and pilot a remote, voice-based standardized patient (SP) method for evaluating an intake chatbot's history-taking, documentation, and patient-centeredness. Methods: Four primary care cases had Easy and Difficult variants. In Phase 1, five SPs completed 40 encounters with internal medicine residents rating portrayal fidelity.
